published_prior_art.cite: ChenSantAnnaXie2025 derives conditional-covariance EIFs for staggered DiD, while AkbariKiyavashGhassami2025 gives canonical two-period DDD EIFs; neither covers their joint eligibility-by-cohort DDD model.

AkbariKiyavashGhassami2025 proves cross-fitted canonical-DDD inference and ChenSantAnnaXie2025 gives efficient staggered-DiD estimation, but neither treats learned joint shared-comparison DDD covariance.
OrtizVillavicencioSantAnna2025 Remark 4.6 gives the constant optimal-GMM combination; ChenSantAnnaXie2025 supplies the analogous conditional-covariance weighting mechanism for staggered DiD.
OrtizVillavicencioSantAnna2025 supplies the constant-GMM comparator; the proposed nondegenerate DDD covariance witness is a concrete specialization of standard conditional-GLS loss geometry.
AiChen2012 gives general sequential-moment efficiency geometry and ChenSantAnnaXie2025 a staggered-DiD closed-form specialization, not the stated DDD shared-comparison block formula.

soundness_flags.label: def:crossfit-estimator and thm:crossfit-attainment
soundness_flags.one_line: The claimed estimator is not yet a defined statistic: neither the empirical tangent projection nor the plug-in normal-equation/Riesz solver is specified (basis, regularization, and solution rule), and the fitted target-share score says it replaces tau_omega although its displayed source formula contains the separate tau_{g,e}'s.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper uses specific not-yet-treated cohorts as comparisons and describes aggregation as optimal GMM based on recentered influence functions with an unconditional population weighting matrix.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 8, Theorem 5 and equation (6); pp. 11–14, cross-fitting discussion and Theorem 10
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives a nonparametric panel-DDD EIF for the canonical two-period setup and gives cross-fitted asymptotic-normality results under positivity and nuisance-rate conditions.
The paper gives staggered-DiD/event-study EIFs using a conditional covariance matrix and an efficient estimator attaining the bound; its model has no eligibility-domain DDD contrast.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Econometrics 170(2), 2012; publisher full text inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article computes semiparametric efficiency bounds for sequential moment restrictions containing unknown functions and presents an optimally weighted orthogonalized sieve minimum-distance estimator.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv preprint corresponding to the cited 2018 Econometrics Journal article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited work is the Double/Debiased Machine Learning treatment-and-structural-parameters paper supplying the generic cross-fitting framework.
Stacked Triple Differences is an available arXiv preprint that explicitly presents stacked DDD as complementary to GMM and as trading efficiency for regression-based transparency.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the abstract plug-in projection with a finite sieve/Riesz construction: declare the basis, empirical inner product, regularizer, fitted derivative, and deterministic root-selection rule; rewrite the trial score explicitly as a function of theta via -theta.

Make the efficient-score theorem operational by resolving the blockwise closed-form projection OEQ, including the full aggregate shared-unit covariance, then show the one-comparison and canonical-DDD reductions directly from that formula.

Demote the fixed-GMM identity to a corollary unless it is extended to the aggregate joint-covariance frontier against both OrtizVillavicencioSantAnna2025 constant GMM and ChenSantAnnaXie2025 conditional weighting.

recommended_next_step: Continue revision on this angle: first make the cross-fitted projection and estimating equation mathematically executable, then retain the field-tier EIF/attainment kernel and its DDD-specific comparison.
